dates.notes: Code of Practice launched on 4 April 2025 and updated on 23 October 2025. The GOV.UK page lists 27 supporting States in the October 2025 version. It is a voluntary, non-binding code under the multistakeholder Pall Mall Process.

gaps: Voluntary and non-binding: it creates no treaty obligation, ratification, depositary, monitoring or enforcement.
The supporting-States list is maintained on a GOV.UK page with update dates, not a treaty depositary; the record is a snapshot of the 23 October 2025 version.
Only supporting States are recorded. International organisations, industry, academia and civil society participate in the wider Pall Mall Process but are not counted as State supporters.
Kosovo is listed as a supporting State by the UK source. The corpus reproduces the source list and does not thereby imply a position on recognition.
The Code addresses commercial cyber intrusion capabilities; it is not a general cyber-security or cybercrime instrument.

languages.note: English is the published language of the GOV.UK Code. No authentic-language clause.

legal_nature.rationale: A voluntary and non-binding Code of Practice for States. Support is political; the text expressly says it is voluntary and non-binding and creates no treaty obligation.

parties.summary: 27 States are listed as supporting States in the GOV.UK version updated 23 October 2025. Support is political and the Code is expressly voluntary and non-binding.
unknowns: The list is updated on GOV.UK rather than in a treaty depositary; later additions or withdrawals are not reflected after 23 October 2025.

related.note: Both are non-binding, State-support cyber instruments; the Paris Call is a broad multistakeholder declaration, the Pall Mall Code is a State-facing code on commercial intrusion capabilities.

cyber_provisions: Pillar 1 — accountability: controls on the development, facilitation, purchase, transfer and use of commercial cyber intrusion capabilities
Pillar 2 — precision: lawful, necessary and proportionate State use
Pillar 3 — oversight: assessment and due diligence
Pillar 4 — transparency: supply-chain understanding, reporting and review
